title: Heat diffusion in the ground
summary: Soil temperature at depth as the output of a diffusive low-pass system driven by the air: the cycles that drive it, the damping and lag it applies, and the soil properties that set them.

concepts.label: Temperature cycle
concepts.description: A periodic driver of ground temperature at the surface.

concepts.label: Soil temperature
concepts.description: Temperature of a soil layer, °C (here ERA5-Land layer means).

facts.text: ERA5-Land's soil layers are 0–7, 7–28, 28–100 and 100–255 cm.

concepts.label: Frequency response
concepts.description: How a system scales and delays each input frequency.

children.label: Amplitude attenuation
children.description: Output amplitude over input amplitude, e^(−Δz/d) in diffusion.

children.label: Phase lag
children.description: Delay of the output cycle, Δz/d radians in diffusion; at most 90° for one first-order stage.

children.label: Damping depth
children.description: d = √(2κ/ω), the e-folding depth of a cycle.

concepts.label: Soil thermal properties
concepts.description: What sets the filter: diffusivity κ, from conductivity, density and heat capacity.

children.label: Thermal diffusivity
children.description: κ in m²/s; typical soils 0.2–0.8 mm²/s.

children.label: Soil moisture
children.description: Water content, which raises conductivity and heat capacity.

children.label: Snow cover
children.description: An insulating layer that decouples soil from air in winter.
